potentiometers.title: Choose the pot, then the cap
potentiometers.body:
A control has at least four independently important geometries: the visible cap or bare shaft, the panel bushing and fastening hardware, the body behind the panel, and the terminals/footprint. Shrinking one does not shrink the others.

The original ALPS RK09L1140A5L research was useful for a metal-shaft, threaded-bushing assembly. The later Bourns PTV09A-4020F family removed the panel nut and used a capless insulated shaft. Neither is universally better: a panel-clamped control and a board-supported control distribute operating loads differently. The front panel and PCB supports must be designed accordingly.

### Electrical value is not a mechanical choice

B103, B104 and B504 correspond to nominal 10 kΩ, 100 kΩ and 500 kΩ in the selected Bourns family. The shaft geometry is shared; loading and leakage sensitivity are not. A buffered divider, attenuator, OTA control-current network and RC timing rheostat may need different values or tapers.

For a simple divider across a stable voltage, the unloaded midpoint source resistance is at most approximately one quarter of the total resistance. A high-impedance receiver helps preserve the divider law; finite bias current and contamination can still introduce offset.

### DC ratings matter in a bipolar synth

The Bourns family source lists 20 V DC maximum operating voltage. The retained ALPS source distinguishes a 10 V DC limit from its AC rating. Connecting a control end-to-end across −12 V and +12 V creates **24 V**, not 12 V. A buffered lower-voltage control domain is a possible design response; it must be designed rather than assumed.

### What a purchase specification needs

Specify manufacturer and complete suffix, resistance, taper, detent option, shaft form and length, bushing, terminal configuration and the permitted factory process. A cap adds bore shape, insertion depth, retention and skirt clearance. A mechanical coupon should check usable shaft reach, operating force and the real nut/washer/tool envelope.

Sources: [Bourns PTV09](https://www.bourns.com/docs/product-datasheets/PTV09.pdf), [ALPS RK09L1140A5L](https://tech.alpsalpine.com/e/products/detail/RK09L1140A5L/). The corresponding profiles retain source files and model status separately.

faders.title: Fader travel, body length and illuminated stems
faders.body:
The fader study is worth keeping even though the instrument changed to rotary controls. It exposed a common layout failure: rendering the travel length as though it were the whole part.

The ALPS RS20H111C009 has 20 mm travel in a nominal 35 mm body. Its lever has a finite dimension along that travel. In a top-view study, the swept opening is approximately **travel + stem length along motion + chosen end clearances**. It is not simply the travel value. A cap can require an even larger sweep, and the body, lugs and solder lands occupy a different envelope.

The Bourns PTL20 family also has a nominal 35 mm body for its 20 mm travel. Its 10/15/19 mm lever choices describe height, not different travel lengths. Selecting a shorter lever can change reach through the faceplate without recovering length along the panel.

### An illuminated control is two electrical functions

The potentiometer and LED are independent circuit elements. For an envelope generator, the pot can set the time while the LED is driven from a buffered envelope and a stage-enable signal. The light should not load a timing capacitor or become a proxy for the mechanical wiper position.

The exact PTL candidate was a green-LED variant. An amber drawing does not establish an amber orderable suffix. Record LED terminals, polarity, current, brightness and thermal limits independently.

### Why the instrument changed to pots

R12 traded faders for small pots with separate LEDs to reduce footprint and sourcing/assembly effort. That is an instrument-specific decision, not a finding that faders are unsuitable for synths. The SE1 photograph remained an identification lead because its exact BOM row was not established.

Sources: [ALPS RS20H111C009](https://tech.alpsalpine.com/e/products/detail/RS20H111C009/), [Bourns PTL](https://www.bourns.com/docs/product-datasheets/PTL.pdf), [Weston DIY references](https://www.westonaudio.com/diy.html).

panel-stack.title: A flat panel can use several PCB mounting depths
panel-stack.body:
The panel, selected hardware and PCB planes form one mechanical design. They must be solved together before routing. Mechanical testing confirms the intended stack; it should not be the first time the team discovers that a jack mouth is buried behind the panel.

For a threaded patch jack, begin at the panel: the body remains behind it, the bushing passes through a normal hole, and the nut clamps the intended shoulder/stack. Do not raise the entire panel to clear a tall rotary selector and then enlarge every jack hole to admit a plug barrel.

A useful axial relationship is:

```text
exposed actuator = PCB-to-tip height − PCB-to-panel-underside spacing − panel thickness
```

For threaded parts this must be accompanied by shoulder support, washer/nut thickness, thread engagement and tolerance. Catalogue shaft length often uses a different datum from PCB-to-tip height.

### Separate board planes

Group parts by compatible mechanical stack: jack boards, small-pot boards, rotary-selector adapters, toggle strips, near-panel LED/button boards, and a rear circuit board. Not every function needs its own board, and boards at different depths need clearance in all three axes. Hidden PCB windows or notches are different from oversized front-panel holes.

A header/socket or factory-terminated harness can connect these assemblies. Use spacers and panel/support fasteners to carry insertion force and torque. Neither long pin joints nor tightening the panel nuts until the PCB bends is a valid height adjustment.

### What is reusable from the project

The fixed-centre SRBV selector adaptation and split jack-board construction are instructive case studies, not universal board outlines. The corpus retains their component constraints without importing the instrument's board coordinates as a standard.

Sources: [ALPS selector](https://tech.alpsalpine.com/e/products/detail/SRBV160803/), [Bourns shaft drawings](https://www.bourns.com/docs/product-datasheets/PTV09.pdf), [Thonk jack family](https://www.thonk.co.uk/shop/thonkiconn/). See the source-history page for the pinned project decision documents.

toggle-functions.title: Toggle positions, contacts and readable labels
toggle-functions.body:
A switch must be selected from its electrical truth table and its mechanical assembly, not from a generic rectangle in a preview.

| Function | Maintained positions | Design implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LFO / VCO | Two | ON–ON SPDT can encode the two ranges |
| SOFT / OFF / HARD | Three | ON–OFF–ON needs a defined centre-open response |
| ASR / AR / LOOP | Three | Centre-open can mean AR if the circuit defines it |
| Linear / curved envelope | Two | Two states; no invented third browser position |
| Rise / fall stage gate | Two | Select a stage signal; this is not envelope mode |

C908280 refers to the two-position Dailywell candidate. The three-position T1 counterpart is a different complete ordering string. A DPDT option adds another pole and may require more body and terminal space; it is not a stock-based substitute for the SPDT footprint.

### Labels are part of the control contract

A waveform can explain slow versus fast range, a straight versus curved envelope, or the active rise/fall segment. SOFT versus HARD sync is less self-evident; a hybrid of symbols and short words is more reliable than inventing a private icon language. Put full meanings in the documentation even when the panel is compact.

### Assembly and sourcing

PCB pins and solder lugs are different products. Confirm the part's pin view, body, bushing, nut/washer, lever length, throw and soldering/cleaning limits. The corpus keeps the source's unresolved suffix evidence visible rather than equating a shop label with all variants.

Sources: [Thonk sub-miniature toggles](https://www.thonk.co.uk/shop/sub-mini-toggle-switches/), [cnōc manual](https://www.instruomodular.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/cno%CC%84c-Manual.pdf). No cnōc circuit is copied or claimed as implemented here.

sample-hold-slew.title: Separate sample storage from the slew output
sample-hold-slew.body:
A sample-and-hold captures a target voltage. A slew stage controls how the output approaches that target. Keeping the two separate avoids corrupting the held charge while adjusting the glide.

```text
protected/conditioned trigger → acquisition pulse
                                      ↓
conditioned IN → sample-and-hold → buffer → variable lag → buffer → OUT
                       ↓
                local hold capacitor
```

The LF398 tracks while its sampling control is asserted. A long gate applied directly therefore produces tracking rather than a single short acquisition. The CD74HC221 one-shot proposal addresses that distinction, but the pulse width still has to exceed acquisition needs under the chosen capacitor, step and accuracy conditions.

### Storage error and timing

For an ideal capacitor, a leakage current produces droop approximately `dV/dt = I/C`. Increasing C reduces that contribution but usually increases acquisition time. Offset, hold step, dielectric absorption, board leakage and temperature add separate errors. Room-temperature typical figures are not long-hold pitch guarantees.

The LF398M/NOPB package is SOIC-14, distinct from the eight-pin DIP option. Keep the exact pin map and the sensitive storage node on a local clean PCB region; do not put the hold capacitor or that node on a harness.

### The two-knob slew proposal

The R21 starting point used 500 kΩ linear resistance, a 2.2 kΩ minimum series resistance and nominal 0.50 µF lag capacitance, **after** the storage buffer. The ideal time constant is:

```text
tau = (2.2 kohm + R_slew) × 0.50 microfarad
nominal tau range = 1.1 ms to 251.1 ms
```

This is exponential lag, not constant-rate linear slew and not an exact reproduction of ADDAC215. FAST retains some lag. A new sample during a transition updates the destination from the current output level. The indicator should show the final slewed output.

Sources: [TI LF398](https://www.ti.com/lit/gpn/lf398-n), [TI CD74HC221](https://www.ti.com/product/CD74HC221), [ADDAC215](https://www.addacsystem.com/en/products/modules/addac200-series/addac215).

mixers-attenuverters.title: Attenuverter, offset, sum and VCA are different operations
mixers-attenuverters.body:
Four useful functions should not be collapsed under a vague ATTEN label.

An **attenuator** scales a signal toward zero. An **attenuverter** also permits polarity inversion. An **offset** adds a voltage. A **VCA** makes gain respond to a control signal. Each has a different signal path, control law and failure behavior.

For an attenuator/offset cell, the proposed relationship was:

```text
OUT = gain × IN + manual_offset + OFFSET_CV
```

The input-gain control does not also scale the separately added offset. For a mixer with post-sum gain:

```text
SUM = VCA_gain × (g1×IN1 + g2×IN2 + g3×IN3 + g4×IN4)
```

ATTEN CV controls that final gain. It is neither a fifth audio input nor an offset added directly to the audio sum.

### Headroom must be checked at every stage

Reducing post-sum gain cannot undo clipping that already occurred in the summing amplifier. A useful CLIP indication needs either multiple observation points or a justified worst-case relationship between the monitored node and all relevant internal headroom.

Op-amp voltage swing, resistor tolerances, bias and reference errors affect the real gain and offset. A centre mark on a pot is not an electrical zero guarantee. VCA control conditioning must enforce safe OTA bias currents where LM13700 is used.

### Panel relationships

Solid lines can show signal combination and dashed lines can show parameter control, provided the distinction is documented. They must not imply default patch connections between independent modules. Physical group separators remain a third, separate layer.

Sources: [LM13700](https://www.ti.com/product/LM13700), [OPA4196](https://www.ti.com/product/OPA4196), [ADDAC203 interaction reference](https://www.addacsystem.com/en/products/modules/addac200-series/addac203-rev02). Equations above describe the proposed functions, not measured circuits.

amplifier-choice.title: Choose amplifier performance and power together
amplifier-choice.body:
A large analog instrument multiplies seemingly modest per-amplifier costs. Four sections in each package, repeated across buffers, indicators, mixers and references, can dominate the rail budget before any external load is driven.

The source research distinguished OPA4196IDR for many general stages from OPA4197IPWR for precision functions. Earlier TL074-family suggestions remain useful comparisons, not interchangeable identities.

### Compare the operating point, not a marketing adjective

Record input common-mode range, output swing at load, input bias and offset over temperature, noise, bandwidth, slew rate and quiescent current. A rail-to-rail description does not establish the same swing for every load. A typical picoamp input current at room temperature does not bound a hot, contaminated high-impedance assembly.

Use exact package and pin maps. SOIC-14 and TSSOP-14 are different footprints even if the logical channel arrangement is familiar.

### Precision output stages

An output resistor can help limit fault current and isolate cable capacitance. Taking feedback after that resistor can improve loaded DC accuracy while changing loop stability. The compensation network must remain one fixed configuration across the complete load/cable sweep, then be checked on a populated circuit. A model sweep is not physical qualification.

### A practical rail ledger

For each fitted package, account for all powered amplifier sections at the relevant limits, plus output current, indicator drive, bias/reference loads, protection, regulators and charging currents. Keep the typical estimate separate from the conservative design bound. Multiply per-channel values only once; do not confuse them with per-package values.

Sources: [OPA4196](https://www.ti.com/product/OPA4196), [OPA4197](https://www.ti.com/product/OPA4197), [TL074](https://www.ti.com/product/TL074). The original instrument's power and model results remain contextual evidence, not universal specifications for these amplifiers.

indicator-design.title: Magnitude, clipping and envelope stage indication
indicator-design.body:
An LED can communicate several different quantities. Specify which before drawing a light beside every jack.

**Magnitude** indication should observe a buffered signal, with an appropriate rectifier/envelope response when both CV and audio are expected. Equal positive and negative magnitudes can intentionally produce equal brightness; that is not a polarity indicator.

**CLIP** indication needs a threshold related to actual circuit headroom. It is not just a brighter magnitude LED. If a VCA follows a summing stage, monitor upstream clipping as well as the final output where required.

**Stage** indication combines two signals: the generated envelope level and the active rise/fall state. The RISE light may brighten during rise and the FALL light dim during fall; both can be off during sustain even though ENV remains high. The pots set durations, not LED brightness directly.

### Electrical and optical design are inseparable

A small 0402 package may clear a dense PCB while a large light window remains on the faceplate. That still needs a controlled optical path: direct near-panel emitter, diffuser or lightpipe, with no unwanted bleed. Package height can differ between white and red LEDs with similar footprints.

Current must be bounded during normal, startup, tolerance and fault conditions. Use maximum supply, minimum relevant forward voltage and resistor tolerance for a first current screen, then the resistor/LED derating at installed hot ambient. An absolute maximum is not an operating target.

### Layout lesson

Put the emitter/driver where it fits and route the indicator artwork around the real aperture and component keepout. Do not tuck an LED into a corner because it looks empty in a top view while the pot body occupies that volume below.

Sources: retained Kingbright [white](https://www.kingbrightusa.com/images/catalog/SPEC/APHHS1005QWF-D.pdf) and [red](https://www.kingbrightusa.com/images/catalog/SPEC/APG1005SEC-E-T.pdf) documents; exact acquired-byte records are in the source manifest.

patch-protection.title: Protect inputs, outputs and the powered-off instrument
patch-protection.body:
A patchable instrument must be considered in combinations its internal schematic alone cannot predict: external voltage on an input, two outputs patched together, a connected source while this instrument is off, a missing rail, or an unexpected return path through a cable sleeve.

ADG5412F is relevant to input fault isolation, but its protected behavior applies to named terminals and supply conditions. Correctly protecting inputs does not automatically protect amplifier outputs, precision feedback sense paths or reference receivers.

### Keep a fault-path inventory

For each external port, trace where current flows under opposite-drive, powered-off and partial-rail conditions. Include output resistors, clamp diodes, protection switches, internal ESD paths, rail capacitance and any sense lead that bypasses a series resistor.

A TVS is a transient component with specified test conditions. It is not a guarantee against arbitrary sustained overvoltage. A PTC has time- and temperature-dependent behavior, not an immediate perfect current limit. A clamp to a dead rail can power unintended circuitry.

### Return continuity

A patch sleeve must not become the sole intended power return. Parallel grounds can divide current unevenly. Rail-only sensing cannot necessarily distinguish an intact power return from a failed return being replaced by an external cable.

### Scope of this corpus

This is an evidence-led design checklist, not a complete protection circuit or safety certification. The source project's later protection and external-supply requirements are deliberately retained as unresolved engineering work. No raw-to-load abstract boundary in a diagram is a real protective device.

Sources: [ADG5412F](https://www.analog.com/en/products/adg5412f.html), [LM74502](https://www.ti.com/product/LM74502), and the pinned project protection decisions linked from the history page.

interconnects.title: Factory-complete connections between separate boards
interconnects.body:
The no-home-soldering requirement permits ordinary synth components and separate PCBs. What it requires is that every electrical joint be completed before delivery.

A rigid header/socket pair can work where boards overlap and its engaged height fits the mounting stack. A terminated, keyed harness can work between side-by-side boards or where several mounting depths must be bridged. Straight pins cannot join non-overlapping boards without an intermediate backplane or a different connector arrangement.

### A connector is a system

Keep the board header, cable housing, contact, wire, termination tool/process and inspection criteria as separate identities. The JST GH records demonstrate this: a housing or loose crimp contact is not a PCB-mounted component. Some source footprints are explicitly numbering aids and must not be fabricated as actual housing land patterns.

Specify pin count, numbering view, mating pair, polarity/keying, conductor gauge, insulation range, engagement, latch access and strain relief. A socket body height is not the complete board separation. Do not assign mating status from similar pitch alone.

### Electrical requirements

Account for contact and wire resistance, permissible voltage drop, loaded contact heating and return-current distribution. Local sensitive nodes such as an S&H hold capacitor should not travel through a harness; buffer them first. Constrain cable length and capacitance where an amplifier drives the connection.

Mechanical supports must carry torque, insertion force and cable pull. Mating connectors are not a substitute for the board's structural mounting plan.

Sources: [JST GH family](https://www.jst-mfg.com/product/detail_e.php?series=105), [Samtec SSW](https://www.samtec.com/products/ssw), [Samtec TSW](https://www.samtec.com/products/tsw). The corpus keeps the original JST PDF and Alpha Wire documents with their hashes.

power-budget.title: Do not infer full-instrument power from a preview
power-budget.body:
The early playground previews reused the concept of zudo-pd. Later circuit enumeration showed why a visible power-board pocket is not a completed supply design.

A useful ledger separates quiescent IC demand, signal/load current, reference networks, LEDs, protection/monitoring, optional domains and capacitive startup. Record each rail separately, including the negative rail. Two inlet connectors on one converter do not create two independent power sources.

### Requirements and actual hardware

The later source selected a conditional external regulated-source **requirement**, not an exact purchased supply and inlet. This corpus retains both the earlier P+B research and that later decision without calling the old construction a universally inadequate product or the new boundary a completed circuit.

For any implementation, confirm voltage bands at the load after wire/contact/protection/return drops; transient capability and limiting; sequencing and missing-rail behavior; discharge; thermal conditions; and fault energy. Do not equate a source's minimum current capability with a safe maximum delivered fault current.

### Distribution also needs a model

A heavy return wire can still connect through a narrow PCB neck. Several same-net copper islands do not establish one connected return network. A green schematic or DRC result does not measure milliohm spreading resistance, installed contact temperature or startup behavior.

### USB-PD is an interface, not a complete bipolar supply

The negotiated input, programmed defaults and converter topology determine the resulting rails. Preserve exact board revision and programming state; a bare controller or connector identity does not establish safe operation with an arbitrary charger.

Read the pinned source [supply-architecture decision](https://github.com/Takazudo/zudo-osc-hole-field/blob/fac99297702eabd97bbc3fae58876af4017fcaea/doc/src/content/docs/decisions/osc-supply-architecture.mdx). It is a project case study, not an order recommendation.

noise-sources.title: Noise source, color shaping and output buffers
noise-sources.body:
The noise block began as one white output and grew to white, pink, blue and brown. These are useful circuit responsibilities to preserve independently of the panel tile.

Electric Druid NOISE2 offers programmed white/pink generation. A blank microcontroller with the same package is not equivalent; programmed identity and delivery must be part of the factory bill of materials. This route is digital pseudorandom generation. A reverse-biased analog junction is a different source with its own repeatability, level and noise-characterization work.

### Shaping within a defined band

Ideal white noise has flat power spectral density. Pink has less high-frequency power; blue has more; brown has a stronger low-frequency weighting. Practical colored-noise outputs must define a useful frequency band and level rather than claiming an ideal spectrum down to DC and up to infinity.

One proposal was leaky/band-limited integration of white for brown and bounded differentiation of pink for blue. The leakage and bandwidth limits prevent uncontrolled DC drift or excessive high-frequency gain. These are proposed topologies, not measured filters or proof of exact coloration.

### Independent outputs

Buffer each output so patch loading does not change the others or the shaping network. Define common level/headroom targets and test spectra, clipping, startup and correlation as appropriate to the musical use.

The corpus retains the NOISE2 source and a separate record for the analog-source direction. It does not invent transistor avalanche ratings or call a noise-colored panel label a finished circuit.

Source: [Electric Druid NOISE2](https://electricdruid.net/product/noise2-white-pink-generator/), with the original manufacturer PDF retained in the source archive.

factory-assembly.title: No soldering at home is a delivery requirement
factory-assembly.body:
JLCPCB preference and no-home-soldering are related but different constraints. The first chooses a sourcing/assembly route; the second defines the state in which the instrument's electrical assemblies must arrive.

Standard potentiometers, toggles, faders, jacks, programmed devices and externally sourced parts can still satisfy the requirement when the factory accepts their exact procurement and assembly operations. A catalogue entry is not an accepted order, and distributor stock is not reserved PCBA stock.

### Specify the complete delivered assembly

Include soldered through-hole parts, both sides of board connectors, terminated cables, programmed components, any alignment fixture, electrical inspection and the agreed calibration. No adapter or board-to-board joint should quietly be deferred to the user's soldering iron.

Mechanical final assembly—nuts, screws, board supports and plugging completed connectors—can remain separate if that is the agreed delivery arrangement. Full enclosure integration needs its own accepted scope; it cannot be inferred from ordinary PCB assembly service.

### Processes can constrain the part choice

Check the exact component's solder profile, wash restrictions, masking and heat exposure. A plastic actuator that clears the panel may still be incompatible with the assumed assembly process. Ask about the actual orientation and fixture needed for tall or heavy through-hole parts.

### Prototype without committing the whole instrument

A small factory-assembled mechanical coupon can exercise the real jack/nut/panel, pot shaft, rotary selector, toggle, button/plunger and LED optical path. A separate electrical coupon can test a complete oscillator or sample/hold/slew channel. Preserve failures and setup conditions, not only successful photographs.

Source route: [JLCPCB assembly FAQ](https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/pcb-assembly-faqs). Service scope and availability require rechecking at the quotation/order stage; this corpus submits no quote or order.

model-fidelity.title: What a 3D preview proves—and what it does not
model-fidelity.body:
The corpus keeps original CAD, derived browser geometry and physical qualification separate.

| Class | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Manufacturer-supplied | Acquired from the identified product/family source; suffix and drawing agreement still need review |
| Family/community | Useful shared geometry, not proven exact to the selected variant |
| Derived | A recorded transformation of a source, including tessellation or a drawing-based proxy |
| Unavailable | No usable model; no placeholder is presented as an acquired model |

Most native package previews inherited from the instrument are small, drawing-derived envelope models. They intentionally lack some detail. They must not be mistaken for full manufacturer solids. The recovered ALPS pot and fader STEP files provide more detailed source geometry, while the PJ398SM model remains a community family reference.

### This edition's STEP path

The local conversion script tessellates the original STEP with CadQuery/OpenCascade and records input hash, output hash, tool versions, tessellation parameters, triangle count and bounds. It does not edit the original. The browser mesh is a derived viewing asset, not a new exact-vendor STEP or a drilling template.

The standard zudo-circuit-doc viewer remains responsible for the published WRL package previews. The supplementary hardware viewer handles these additional STEP-derived meshes without putting unselected files into the generator-owned model directory.

### A usable mechanical check

Verify units, axes, origin, mounting plane, full envelope, terminal detail, rotation and scale against the drawing. A render can expose a mismatch; it cannot prove thread engagement, cap retention, tolerance stack or strength. Use the exact model receipt and source drawing before designing around it.

Datasheets and vendor CAD retain their original rights. The package is a local research archive; copying a source into it does not grant public redistribution rights.

source-workflow.title: A corpus is not a bill of materials
source-workflow.body:
This side project selects information for documentation, not components for a new fabricated board. All imported inventory lines are marked not fitted and have no declared placements. The original instrument inventory is preserved separately for provenance.

Each profile distinguishes source identity, acquisition, inherited verdicts, current research commentary, model fidelity and assembly status. A part rejected from one compact layout may be excellent in a different instrument. A known name or catalogue code is not a universal approval.

### Evidence layers

The authored profiles explain why a part matters and what to investigate. The native generated pages project the inherited exact-component bundles. Original source documents and CAD live outside public assets, with hashes and acquisition context. Historical candidates stay in research instead of being silently promoted to exact manufacturing selections.

An inherited `PASS` means the originating evidence record made a scoped claim at its recorded locator. It is not a new bench result, a present stock guarantee or this corpus's blanket endorsement. `SOURCE UNAVAILABLE` and identity gaps remain visible.

### Updating the corpus

Start from the complete manufacturer/MPN/package identity. Acquire and inspect the actual source bytes, record the URL/date/hash and exact locator, then update only the claims it supports. A family model can be reused as family geometry; it cannot acquire exact-vendor fidelity by renaming the file.

Use the canonical `circuit/WORKFLOW.md` for component promotion and generated output. Edit research profiles or source evidence, then regenerate; do not hand-edit `doc/src/content/docs/components/`.

### Public versus local assets

The source pack is retained for local research. The build deliberately links original document URLs. Review third-party terms before publishing raw vendor files or derived previews publicly. No site has been deployed and no hardware order is authorized by this corpus.
